messages.subject: difference in Likelihood between 0.4-14 and 0.5-16
parts:
So, I have a question regarding version differences. I know that somewhere along the line in fitting SEMs with single regression relationships. Although it seems to extend to other multi-regression relationships as well. And it’s changed the order of AIC values for some analyses, which is causing me a bit of consternation.

Below I’m including some test code. What I want to know is, is the 0.4 or the 0.5 answer correct? Then we can go forward with our work. Here’s the toy example.

#AICc toy problem: AIC and likelihood in Lavaan .5-15 vs .4-14
rm(list=ls())
library(lavaan)
library(AICcmodavg)



set.seed(2002)
adf <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100), x1 = rnorm(100), y1 = rnorm(100), y2 = rnorm(100))
head(adf)


adf$x.2<-adf$x^2

mod1 <- '
y2 ~ x + 0*x1 + 0*y1 + 0*x.2
#y1 ~ 0*x1 + x
'
fit1 <- sem(mod1, data=adf)
summary(fit1,fit.measures=TRUE)


#Running this in 0.4-14 gives the following
# log likelihood, user model: -110899.869
# log likelihood, unrestricted model: -729.827
# AIC: 221803.737 (K = 2)

#Running this in 0.5-15 gives the following
# log likelihood, user model: -731.850
# log likelihood, unrestricted model: -729.827
# AIC: 1467.699 (K = 2)

#NOTES: rm(list=ls()) has to be used between version runs.
# Seems to have something to do with
# only one model (i.e., ~ regression): adding in the y1 portion of the model/code solves the problem
# nonlinear terms

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: difference in Likelihood between 0.4-14 and 0.5-16
parts:
On 03/11/2014 03:17 PM, Jarrett Byrnes wrote:
> Below I'm including some test code. What I want to know is, is the
> 0.4 or the 0.5 answer correct?

It took me a while to figure this one out (0.4-14 does not run with R >
3.0; I had to downgrade R). But the answer is: 0.5 is correct. -731.850
it must be.

0.4-14 screwed this one up, but AFAICS, only if a single equation was
involved.

Beware that in 0.6 (not ready any time soon), this will change again.
The logl for H0 in this case will be -128.907. Because we should ignore
the (fixed) exogenous covariates (if fixed.x=TRUE) when calculating the
log likelihood.

Yves.
